The broader project includes a 6 MW solar power plant and a 15 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), supporting the use of clean energy beyond household electricity consumption. ANI Updated On Oct 10, 2026 at 01:45 PM IST Gujarat’s Modhera expands solar-powered living to green mobility Modhera, known as India's first 24x7 solar-powered village, is extending its clean-energy initiative towards green mobility, with residents adopting electric vehicles and solar-powered charging infrastructure supporting the transition. Under Solar Village Modhera 2.0, the village is integrating renewable energy with everyday transportation. The broader project includes a 6 MW solar power plant and a 15 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), supporting the use of clean energy beyond household electricity consumption. Advt An electric vehicle charging station has also been established near the Sun Temple, allowing residents to charge their vehicles using solar-generated electricity. "An electric vehicle charging station has also been set up near the Solar Temple, with its power supply coming from the solar ground-mounted power plant. People can use it to charge their vehicles, helping them save on petrol and diesel and reduce carbon emissions. This charging station provides an additional benefit to the community," said Dilip Kumar, Deputy Engineer at Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited (GUVNL). articles.title: Jio Says India Could Be Among First Countries To Launch 6G By 2030, Reveals New Technology
articles.content: Jio Prepares For India’s 6G Revolution Reliance Jio has said India could become one of the first countries in the world to roll out commercial 6G services when global standards are finalised in 2030. The telecom operator showcased its latest pre-6G technologies at the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi, signalling its ambition to play a leading role in the next generation of wireless connectivity. The company has developed a proprietary pre-6G technology stack and a new Giga MIMO Radio , which it describes as India’s first. Jio also demonstrated a common baseband unit designed to support both 5G and future 6G networks. 6G Could Deliver Five Times The Capacity Of 5G According to Jio, future 6G networks could offer up to five times the capacity of current 5G networks while reducing latency by nearly ten times. Higher capacity would allow networks to handle substantially more data and connected devices. Lower latency could make applications that require almost instantaneous responses more practical. Potential applications include real-time artificial intelligence, holographic video communications, remote healthcare and digital education. These capabilities could also support industrial automation and other services requiring rapid data exchange. However, these are expected capabilities rather than performance figures from a commercially deployed Indian 6G network. Actual results will depend on the technology, spectrum and standards eventually adopted. What Is Jio’s Giga MIMO Radio? A major highlight of Jio’s showcase at IMC 2026 was its Giga MIMO Radio technology. MIMO, or Multiple-Input Multiple-Output, uses multiple antennas to transmit and receive data more efficiently. Advanced versions can improve network capacity and spectral efficiency, particularly in areas with large numbers of users. Jio’s Giga MIMO Radio is part of its effort to develop the hardware required for future-generation networks within India. The common baseband unit showcased alongside it is designed to support both 5G and 6G deployments, potentially making it easier for operators to transition to newer network technologies. Jio Has Filed More Than 8,000 Patents Jio said it has filed more than 8,000 patents, including hundreds related specifically to 6G technologies. The company has also made more than 934 technical contributions to international standardisation bodies as it seeks to influence the global framework for next-generation connectivity. These efforts cover four major areas: hardware development, software architecture, intellectual property and global standards. The work is significant because 6G is still being developed internationally. Companies that contribute technology and research during the standardisation process could be better positioned when commercial networks begin to emerge. AI And Quantum-Safe Networks In Focus Jio expects 6G to make AI-powered services more responsive, particularly in areas where rapid data processing and low-latency feedback are essential. At IMC 2026, the company highlighted possible applications in agriculture, healthcare and education. Jio is also working on AI-native network architectures, in which artificial intelligence is integrated into network operations, and quantum-safe security technologies intended to protect communications against emerging computing threats. These developments reflect a broader industry effort to combine faster connectivity with more intelligent and secure network infrastructure....

articles.title: Heavy rain submerges ancient burial urns at Adichanallur excavation site - DT Next
articles.content: CHENNAI: More than 10 ancient burial urns at the Adichanallur archaeological site in Thoothukudi district have been submerged in rainwater following recent showers, raising concerns over the safety of historically significant artefacts unearthed by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). According to a Daily Thanthi report, the incident has also drawn attention to the slow progress of permanent roofing work at the excavation site, with concerns mounting ahead of the northeast monsoon. Adichanallur, located on the banks of the Thamirabarani river, is an important archaeological site where the ASI conducted excavations four years ago. A site museum was established to enable visitors to view ancient burial urns and other artefacts in their original locations. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman inaugurated India's first site museum at Adichanallur on August 6, 2023, and laid the foundation stone for a world-class museum. However, construction of the proposed museum has remained stalled for various reasons. The excavation area was divided into three zones A, B and C. Excavations at Site C, where a large number of artefacts were discovered, were carried out under temporary roofing. Although work to install a permanent roof in this section has commenced, progress has been slow. The lack of adequate protection has left the excavation pits and the artefacts exposed to changing weather conditions. Recent heavy rainfall in the area caused water to accumulate in the excavation pits, leaving more than 10 ancient burial urns submerged. The situation has raised fears that prolonged exposure to water could damage the urns and the historical materials preserved inside them. The incident has renewed concerns over the maintenance of the archaeological site and the need to protect the remains from further deterioration. Writer Muthalankurichi Kamarasu alleged that the ASI had failed to ensure proper maintenance of the artefacts, leaving them exposed to the sun and rain. He urged officials to expedite the construction of a permanent shelter before the Northeast Monsoon intensifies and take immediate steps to drain the accumulated rainwater and safeguard the archaeological remains.

articles.title: Assam's Putul Sonowal Creates History, Assures India's First -Ever Medal at World Bowls ...
articles.content: Assam’s Putul Sonowal Creates History, Assures India’s First-Ever Medal at World Bowls Champion of Champions Assam Daily News International By NKTV Digital Last updated Oct 10, 2026 18 Share Assam’s Putul Sonowal has created history by assuring India its first-ever medal at the World Bowls Champion of Champions in Barham, Australia. The 43-year-old lawn bowls player secured the historic achievement by advancing to the semi-finals of the men’s singles event. Sonowal booked his place in the last four after defeating Singapore’s Harriman Yuen in the quarter-finals, marking a significant milestone for Indian lawn bowls on the international stage. A member of the Assam Police, Sonowal has emerged as one of India’s leading players in the sport. His latest achievement further highlights his growing stature in international lawn bowls and brings recognition to Assam. Sonowal has enjoyed an impressive run in international competitions. At the 2026 Asian Lawn Bowls Championship, he clinched the gold medal in the men’s singles event, strengthening his position among the leading players in the discipline. Earlier, at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Sonowal registered another notable victory by defeating Canada’s Ryan Bester in the men’s singles event. Bester is a three-time Commonwealth Games medallist and a former world outdoor champion. The contest between Sonowal and Bester went into a tie-break after both players won one set each. Sonowal eventually prevailed, securing an important victory against the experienced Canadian player. Sonowal’s progression to the semi-finals of the World Bowls Champion of Champions has now guaranteed India a historic medal at the prestigious competition. His performance is a significant achievement for Indian lawn bowls and a proud moment for Assam. With a place in the semi-finals secured, all eyes will now be on Sonowal as he looks to continue his impressive campaign and add another milestone to his growing list of achievements.
